 Detroit Lions HC Dan Campbell details defensive improvements, full-circle moment ahead of Dolphins game
 Campbell also gave an update on the health of Jack Campbell and how the team will honor him
 Brandon Carr , Digital Content Producer
 Published:  November 8, 2026 at 5:00 AM Tags:  Detroit Lions , Dan Campbell , Alim McNeill , D.J. Reed Jr. , D.J. Wonnum , Cade Mays , Kerby Joseph , Brian Branch , Amik Robertson , Ennis Rakestraw Jr. , Rock Ya-Sin , Brad Holmes , Anthony Lucas , Michigan Wolverines , Derrick Moore , Blake Miller , Jack Campbell Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell praised the impact of the team’s interior pass rush, reflected on the experiences that shaped his coaching career, and expressed confidence in the team’s defensive depth as it prepares for Sunday’s road game against the Miami Dolphins. (Copyright 2026 by WDIV ClickOnDetroit - All rights reserved.) What to know: 
 Alim McNeill making an impact: Campbell praised McNeill’s interior pass rush, run defense, and ability to create pressure that opens opportunities for Detroit’s edge rushers. 
 Interior pressure helping the entire defense: McNeill’s ability to push the pocket gives Detroit more options with its four-man rush and additional blitz packages. 
 Campbell reflects on Miami experience: The Lions coach discussed his time as the Dolphins’ interim head coach in 2015, calling it an invaluable learning experience that helped prepare him for his current role. 
 Sean Payton played a major mentorship role: Campbell credited his time working with Payton in New Orleans for helping him develop the knowledge needed to become an NFL head coach. 
 Recommended Videos
 ALLEN PARK, Mich. — Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell praised the impact of the team’s interior pass rush, reflected on the experiences that shaped his coaching career, and expressed confidence in the team’s defensive depth as it prepares for Sunday’s road game against the Miami Dolphins.
 Campbell highlighted Alim McNeill ’s ability to disrupt opposing offenses from the middle of the defensive line, noting that his pressure creates opportunities for Detroit’s edge rushers.
 “When you can get push up the middle, first of all, he shuts down the run,” Campbell said. “But then to be able to get an edge and create pressure and push and make the quarterback move, that helps Hutch and that helps Wom and our other guys.”
 Campbell said the combination of interior pressure and an effective edge rush significantly expands Detroit’s defensive possibilities, both with a traditional four-man rush and when the team sends additional pressure.
 “He’s doing a hell of a job. He’s playing at a high level right now,” Campbell said.
 Past experiences helped shape Campbell as a head coach
 Campbell also reflected on his experience as the interim head coach of the Miami Dolphins, a position he took over during the 2015 season.
 He recalled learning about the opportunity shortly after returning from London, giving him little time to prepare for the responsibilities of leading a team during the season.
 Campbell described the experience as challenging but invaluable, especially because he had to learn on the job without an offseason to build his program.
 “I grew a ton from it,” Campbell said. “I’m fortunate that I was given the opportunity because had I not, I probably wouldn’t be sitting in this seat right now.”
 Although Campbell did not receive the permanent position in Miami, he said the experience helped him understand the responsibilities and challenges of being a head coach.
 That knowledge became particularly valuable when he joined Sean Payton’s staff in New Orleans. 
 Campbell credited Payton with helping fill gaps in his understanding of the position and serving as an outstanding mentor.
 “Had I not been able to go with Sean, I wouldn’t be sitting in his seat,” Campbell said.
 Campbell remembers former Miami player Michael Egnew
 Campbell also recalled a moment from his time in Miami that gained attention on HBO’s Hard Knocks , when he challenged tight end Michael Egnew during practice.
 Egnew, a receiving tight end out of Missouri, eventually developed into a physical blocker and even played fullback.
 Campbell remembered Egnew as a player who embraced the position’s demands and gave everything he had.
 “He was tough. He was physical,” Campbell said. “This kid was freaking all heart and toughness, and I appreciate that, man. That dude, he gave everything he had.”
 Lions encouraged by defensive depth despite injuries
 Detroit could be without several key defensive contributors Sunday, including cornerback D.J. Reed Jr. , defensive lineman D.J. Wonnum, offensive lineman Cade Mays and safety Kerby Joseph , with Campbell indicating that those players were unlikely to be available.
 Reed’s potential absence is particularly notable given his recent improvement and growing confidence, Campbell said.
 However, Campbell expressed confidence in the remaining defensive backs, pointing to players including Brian Branch , Amik Robertson , Ennis Rakestraw Jr. , Rock Ya-Sin and others who have continued to contribute.
 Campbell also credited general manager Brad Holmes for building the team’s depth.
 “I just feel like these guys are starting to play pretty good football for us,” Campbell said. “I like where we’re at, and depthwise, we’re pretty strong in that room.”
 With injuries creating additional opportunities along the defensive line, Campbell mentioned Anthony Lucas as another player receiving practice repetitions.
 He also expects former Michigan Wolverines national champion Derrick Moore and other young defensive linemen to benefit from expanded opportunities.
 “Adversity hits with injuries. That’s the tough part, but the encouraging part is now guys get new opportunities,” Campbell said. “You get your chance. And what are you going to do with it?”
 Derrick Moore showing continued development
 Campbell singled out Moore as a player who has continued improving with each opportunity.
 The additional game repetitions have been particularly valuable, giving the young defensive lineman experience that cannot be replicated during practice.
 “There’s no way to duplicate real-time game reps against good opponents, and you see growth,” Campbell said. “I saw growth in practice yesterday.”
 Campbell also praised Moore’s even-keeled personality, describing him as a player who remains composed without lacking intensity.
 He compared Moore’s temperament to that of offensive lineman Blake Miller , saying both players can stay in control and keep learning.
 Campbell described Moore as having a little bit of a “calculated killer” mentality when it comes to football.
 Campbell focused on Sunday’s challenge, not coaching milestones
 Campbell was also asked about the possibility of moving into second place on the Lions’ all-time coaching wins list with a victory Sunday.
 The milestone would break a three-way tie and represent another significant achievement in his tenure in Detroit.
 However, Campbell said he had not given the accomplishment much thought.
 Instead, his attention remains on preparing the team to play its best football and avoid taking a step backward.
 “It’s about us getting better, man. We got to find a way to win this game,” Campbell said. “We got to play our best football, just like we do every week.”
 Team continues to move forward through emotional week
 Campbell closed by addressing the team’s emotional week and updating fans on Jack Campbell’ s continued improvement.
 He said the team has gotten better each day and is developing a stronger understanding of the situation.
 Dan emphasized that the Lions must honor Jack by maintaining their standards in preparation and performance.
 “How would he prepare? How would he play? Those are the standards for us going into this game,” Dan said. “We owe it to him.”
